acceptable_findings.title: No metrics/alerting: payout failures and reconcile drift are only visible in logs
Invariant reconciliation (ops/reconcile.sql) is run manually weekly; not automated or alerted

Outbox relay holds a transaction and row locks while publishing over HTTP (can trip idle_in_transaction_session_timeout; duplicates are deduped downstream), or a permanently rejected row blocks the head of the queue (no attempts or dead-letter column)
Bank idempotency-key retention window is unstated while retries span days
Single outbox relay replica (throughput / availability of event publishing)
No rate limiting at the service (relies on gateway)
Replay returns 201 instead of 200 / response differences on idempotent replay
Payout job processes sellers sequentially (runtime grows with sellers)
Retention/archival plan for ledger_entries and outbox
Missing clearing account makes the payout job fail for that currency
A failed payout has no reversal or requeue path: the money moved to clearing stays there (status 'failed' is never re-selected), and only a log line says so

must_not_flag.claim: Lost update / race on balance_minor = balance_minor + $2
must_not_flag.why_false: The increment runs in a transaction after SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on both accounts, guarded by the unique idempotency key (transfers.py).
UNIQUE (from_account, idempotency_key) claimed first with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; replay with a different body is 409.
UNIQUE (seller_id, payout_date), ledger move in the same transaction, bank Idempotency-Key, CronJob concurrencyPolicy Forbid plus pg_try_advisory_lock.
Transactional outbox written in the same transaction; relay uses FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED.

must_not_flag.claim: SQL injection via f-string in accounts.py
must_not_flag.why_false: The f-string interpolates a module constant (SCOPED); all values are bound parameters.

must_not_flag.claim: Seller can read another seller's account
must_not_flag.why_false: Queries filter by seller_scope taken from the verified JWT; services are unscoped by design; 404 on miss.
asyncpg pool timeout/command_timeout, server-side statement_timeout/lock_timeout/idle_in_transaction timeout, httpx timeouts on bank and bus clients.
Managed PITR 7 days + 30-day snapshots, quarterly restore rehearsal (README, docs/runbooks/restore.md).
readyz acquires with timeout=1 and runs SELECT 1 with timeout=1.

strengths: DB-enforced idempotency keys with request fingerprint
Integer minor units; CHECK constraints for non-negative balances
FOR UPDATE row locks in id order
Transactional outbox + SKIP LOCKED relay with backoff and jitter, SIGTERM handling
Re-runnable payouts: unique per seller/day, bank idempotency key, Forbid + advisory lock
ADR documenting the money design; tested PITR restore
Tests pin replay, concurrency and balance invariants
note: Written as a clean control. Iteration 1 showed it is not fully clean: a baseline run found and reproduced a real deadlock (LC-1), independently re-verified on PostgreSQL 16. Kept unchanged so iterations stay comparable. It now tests both precision (no invented defects) and depth (the subtle real one).

known_real_issues.title: Concurrent transfers deadlock: the transfers INSERT's FK check takes FOR KEY SHARE on both account rows, then SELECT ... FOR UPDATE conflicts with other transactions' key-share locks
known_real_issues.verified: reproduced on PostgreSQL 16: FOR UPDATE -> deadlock detected; FOR NO KEY UPDATE -> both commit

known_real_issues.title: Transfer from/to an unknown account raises a foreign-key violation (500) before the 404 branch
Payout run has no per-seller / per-payout error isolation; an unparseable 2xx from the bank can block the queue
Bank 401/403 (expired token) treated as a permanent per-payout failure, failing every payout in the run
Payouts unique per (seller, date) while balances are per account; no unique (seller_id, currency) for seller accounts
pytest-asyncio strict mode: async fixture declared with plain @pytest.fixture, so DB tests may not run as intended
Restore runbook ignores payouts already sent and sequence rewind (idempotency keys / message ids derived from ids)
Any service token can create any transfer between any accounts (no caller allow-list)
Every component mounts the bank and bus credentials
Append-only ledger not enforced by privileges/triggers
